name: Turso
summary: Turso is a hosted database built on SQLite that can run close to your users anywhere in the world.

free_plan_covers.note: Free plan: 5 GB storage, 500 million monthly row reads, 10 million row writes, and up to 100 databases.

first_paid_usd_month.note: The Developer plan is $4.99/month billed yearly and adds 9 GB storage and 2.5 billion monthly row reads.

portability.note: The client engine and data format (SQLite/libSQL, MIT licensed) are portable, but Turso's newer hosted multitenant server is closed source.

storage_model.note: The main product is a hosted database; an optional local file copy (embedded replica) can sync from it for faster reads.

data_model.note: Turso is built on SQLite/libSQL, a standard SQL database.

realtime_built_in.note: Change tracking features exist but are still marked experimental, so apps cannot yet rely on built-in live push updates.

serverless_friendly.note: The official client talks over HTTP with no native dependencies, built for edge and serverless functions.

mobile_sdk.note: Official SDKs exist for Swift (iOS), Kotlin (Android, preview), and React Native.

setup.step: Install the Turso CLI and sign up or log in from the command line.
Create a database with the CLI.
Get the database URL and an auth token from the CLI.
Add them to your environment file.
Install the client package and connect using the environment variables.

builder_notes: Never expose TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN in client-side code, since it grants full database access.
Use the remote HTTP client in serverless or edge functions, not embedded replicas, since serverless has no persistent local disk.
Use @libsql/client if you need Drizzle or Prisma ORM support; use @tursodatabase/serverless for a lighter, zero-dependency HTTP client.
